What counts as reusable content that you want. I'm a coder not an artist. I've noticed this sub is more artsy but the coding community can be into free use too. Back in the day before everything was git packages and nifty licenses it was just people sharing code segments on forums. I feel like code could evolve better then and code literacy was better. People were interested in the code and what it said more than a downloadable package they can compile without reading.

Free culture focuses on reusable media like photos, video, audio, text, etc. I am also focusing on software because that's really what opened the door. The Creative Commons Share-Alike license is modeled after the GPL.

Free culture artists prefer licenses without restrictions. Generally non-commercial restrictions are not preferred. At this subverse however we are open to posts sharing media with non-commercial and other restrictions. Permission to share like CC no derivatives are ok to post too.

We are also interested in project posts where reusable content is part of the creative output even if the whole project is not reusable.

So, we are not purists. Post what you want. Code is good. Restrictive licenses are ok. The most preferred licenses are public domain, CC0, CC BY (attribution), and CC SA (share-alike) or other similar licenses that allow free reuse.
